description:
feat(contracts): judge meets_intent per guarantee and document part (#2409)

## What

`meets_intent` asked the whole spec one compound question: "Does the document deliver the purpose in the intent, and does every guarantee in the intent have a mechanism in the document?" That one item is always over the decision model's cap, so the 27B read 13k to 36k tokens for a single, interpretive answer.

This PR decomposes it on the grouped fold from #2409 (Judge evidence API v29). Rubric `contract.spec` v10. The label becomes "A guarantee has no mechanism in the document".

## Design as built

**Items.** The registered splitter `contract.guaranteeChunks` emits one item per (guarantee, part).

- **Parts** are of three kinds:
  - the kind's top-level definitions;
  - the rest of the document (the root, which holds `additionalProperties`, security and the stated scope);
  - every decided choice, with `{ decision, why }` as its evidence.
- **The cut:** each guarantee is asked of the 4 parts it names or shares the most terms with, and always of the root.
- **Ordering:** the kept parts are ordered by shared terms. A failing guarantee's note names its first failing part, so it names the most relevant one.
- **Guarantee keys:** an id'd fact uses its id. A grandfathered string uses its first six words plus a 6-hex hash of its text, so inserting another guarantee does not move it.
- **Long strings:** a grandfathered string over the 160-character fact limit is split by sentence.
- **No guarantees:** `meets_intent` has no items and counts toward neither side, and `delivers_purpose` still scores the intent.

**The question asked of each pair:** "Does the document part shown as context make this guarantee hold, through a field, type, operation, header, status code or schema rule it defines, or a behaviour its own text states?" It holds on "yes".

**The fold:** `{ name: 'grouped', groupBy: 'guarantee', inner: 'any', outer: 'all' }`. A guarantee holds when some part makes it hold, and the check holds when every guarantee does.

**Pass-only:** `decisionModel: 'pass-only'`. Clef may pass a pair. A Clef "no" goes to the 27B, whose answer and reason stand, so a failing guarantee always carries a reason. Since #2423, a pass-only `any` group escalates only after all of its Clef answers are in.

**Evidence:** the guarantee is the item's piece. The part and the kind are its shared evidence, so all the guarantees asked of one part pack into one request. Meta holds only the group key and the part.

**What code settles:** code decides which pairs are asked. It settles no guarantee as met or unmet. The candidate rule, "a guarantee naming a definition that does not exist has no mechanism", would be wrong: 126 of 1100 recorded guarantees name in backticks option values such as `whole` and `json`, not definitions.

**Every other check is unchanged.** On all 128 recorded drafts, base and this branch give identical units, questions and folds for `contradicts_guide`, `adds_unasked` and `implements_non_goal`, and identical code-check results. The only difference is TypeScript rendering the absolute path of the tree it ran from inside 14 breaking-change texts. Break ids and counts match.

## `delivers_purpose` (owner's decision: "make it it's own check"; the owner chose this shape)

**Items.** Every sentence of the intent's purpose that is not provenance is a promise. Provenance is a "Provenance:" note, a sentence opening with a version such as "v5 corrects…", or one saying a version "was approved". Each promise is asked of its parts exactly as a guarantee is: the 4 parts it names or shares the most terms with, the decided choices and the root.

**Question:** "Does the document part shown as context make this sentence of the intent's purpose hold, through a field, type, operation, header, status code or schema rule it defines, or a behaviour its own text states?"

**Fold:** grouped by sentence, inner `any`, outer `all`, pass-only.

**Cost.** The part is the same shared evidence `meets_intent` uses, so a part asked by both checks is one Clef request.
- Model-free, per version: Clef requests median 14 → 17, p90 39 → 40. Tokens median 14.7k → 18.7k.
- On the 13 cases, the sum of median seconds per case is 332 s, against 338 s for the outline version (202fdaa4).

**Weight.** The old `meets_intent` weight of 4 is split: `meets_intent` 3, `delivers_purpose` 1. Either miss alone still fails a spec (0.75 or 0.25, under the 0.8 threshold), and the broad purpose carries least.

**Measured** (cand arm, concurrency 1):
- **Positives:** all 13 pass `delivers_purpose` 3/3.
- **Negatives**, `~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/delivers-purpose-negatives.json`, 5 repeats each:

| case | expected | promise shape | main's whole-document check |
|---|---|---|---|
| neg1: unrelated purpose swapped in | no | 0×5 | 0×5 |
| neg2: real purpose plus a zip download nothing provides | no | 0×5 | 0,0,1,1,1 |
| neg3: `POST /sessions/{key}/events` removed from `paths` | no | **1×5 (miss)** | caught 4 of 5 |
| neg3b: removed from `paths`, the root description and its choices | no | **1×5 (miss)** | caught 3 of 5 |
| neg4: purpose reworded, same meaning | yes | 1×5 | 1×5 |

**Known miss.** An operation the purpose promises passes on prose, a choice or a schema that describes it, even though no path defines it. The check's declaration states this. The break gate still catches an operation removed from an approved contract.

A code rule ("a promised METHOD /path the document does not define fails") was measured and rejected. Of 100 operations named in purposes and guarantees across the 159 versions, it flags 30, and all 30 are false failures: a route named as history (`POST /index/facts`), query examples, another surface's routes, and paths written relative to a mount.

**Nothing else moves** on the 128 recorded drafts:
- `contradicts_guide`, `adds_unasked`, `implements_non_goal` and the code checks are identical to main.
- `meets_intent` is identical to 202fdaa4.

## Model-free size

Over 159 versions (128 recorded drafts plus 31 approved specs):

| per version | median | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| guarantees | 6 | 12 | 14 |
| every (guarantee, part) pair | 261 | 430 | 465 |
| pairs asked | 28 | 106 | 190 |
| Clef requests after packing | 14 | 39 | 45 |
| Clef tokens | 14.7k | 45.2k | |

Today the check is 1 27B item of 13k to 36k tokens.

## Replays

All five replays ran 13 cases × 3 repeats in `~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/meets-intent-cases.json`, with base and base2 at fe39c6a1. The cases are:
- 4 versions prod failed;
- 233d9ccf v12, which flipped in an earlier replay;
- 8 passing latest versions.

| replay | cand head | seconds: base / base2 / cand | 27B requests: base / cand | Clef requests (cand) | what changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8e867286 | 1121 / 1198 / 1162 | 39 / 152 | 489 | first build |
| 2 | 726d6451 | 1115 / 1095 / 1105 | 39 / 143 | 489 | a behaviour the part's text states counts |
| 3 | f3578c0f | 1141 / 1067 / 1045 | 39 / 135 | 702 | choices are parts; the root is always asked |
| 4 | 13efe1ff | 1134 / 1160 / **1360** | 39 / 200 | 702 | pass-only alone: +19%, slower |
| 5 | 13efe1ff + #2423 | 1118 / 972 / 1056 | 39 / 102 | 702 | pass-only with the engine fix: inside the base spread |

Cand failures by replay:
- **Replay 1:** cand failed 0c200fa8 v5, aab002bf v25 and 33777f8a v32 on every repeat, where base passes. All 8 cand-only failing guarantees were decided by reasonless Clef "no" answers, from three causes:
  - 4 where the part stated the behaviour but the question accepted only fields and types (fixed in replay 2);
  - 3 held only by a decided choice (fixed in replay 3);
  - 1 where the cut hid the root (fixed in replay 3).
- **Replay 5:**
  - The 3 versions above pass 3/3.
  - Cand fails 33777f8a v1 on every repeat. Base and base2 pass 5 of 6, where prod failed it.
  - 233d9ccf v12 and v13 flip once in three on cand, where both base arms pass 6/6.
  - 608df011 v18 fails on all nine runs.
  - 608df011 v11 and v12 pass 3/3 on cand. Base flips on both.

## Rulings on the disputed versions

Neither arm is ground truth; each ruling is against the spec text.

- **33777f8a v1, "Documents are strict JSON (absent values are null, never optional fields)…": cand is right.** `SealedArtifact` declares `links?: ArtifactLink[]; outcome?: string; summary?: string; basis?: string; carriedFrom?: {…}`, and the document has 76 `?:` fields. The 27B's reason in replay 5 says so, and prod failed v1 on the same guarantee.
- **608df011 v11 and v12: cand is right to pass, and the old check's objection is true.** The objection was "extensions … references #/$defs/service but $defs only defines #/$defs/extension". The code gates already fail both versions on it: `document_clean` reports "does not compile: can't resolve reference #/$defs/service", and `links_resolve` reports "pointer `/$defs/service` is not in the document". `meets_intent` no longer counts it a second time.
- **608df011 v18, `implementerAgent`: every arm fails it, rightly.** The schema lists `implementerAgent` under `github.settings`, so it is accepted rather than "rejected and named".
- **233d9ccf v12 and v13, "At most one event stale: a catalog row reflects the session's latest applied events (Sessions API)": borderline.** The document's "at most one" is the seq gap ("the first event's seq must be at most one past the catalog's watermark…"), and a batch answers `{ acked }`, the highest applied seq. The bound on the catalog row belongs to the Sessions API contract, as the guarantee itself says. The 1-in-3 flip comes from a guarantee this document holds only in part. The fix belongs in the spec, not the judge. Its note now names `POST /sessions/{key}/events` rather than a security scheme.

## Not covered

- **A compound guarantee held across two parts.** 33777f8a v1 "Extensions run in-process in the distributor and mount at /apps/{app}/*; credential-free requests reach only … `pages`, and sessions reach apps with their launch credential" holds across `/App` and `/ExtensionManifest`. Inner `any` asks one part for the whole guarantee. The option I would pick is to also split a grandfathered string over 160 characters at `;`, so each clause is its own guarantee. It is code-only, and the `facts_decomposed` gate already keeps v7 facts to one fact. Not built.
- **"At most one event stale"** stays a borderline cross-contract guarantee, as ruled above.

## Tests

`packages/contracts/test/meets-intent.test.ts` runs against a fake Clef and a scripted judge model. Each new test fails on the head before its change. They cover:
- the cut, with a named part kept and unrelated components left out;
- grouping by guarantee, with the part as shared context;
- requests equal to the number of distinct parts;
- a guarantee holding when one part holds it;
- the check failing with a `guarantee: item: reason` note;
- pass-only, where the judge model's reason stands and its "yes" overturns a Clef "no";
- the wording that counts a stated behaviour;
- choices as parts, and the root always asked;
- parts ordered by relevance;
- stable string keys and the sentence split;
- the purpose standing in when there are no guarantees.

## The final commit, dff3e5c0, supersedes the pass-only design

Replays 1–5 ran the pass-only builds. The final commit moves both checks to one judge-model question per promise, asked with the promise's kept parts (the named or most term-sharing definitions, the decided choices, the root) as its evidence, most relevant first:

- **No decision model.** `decisionModel: false` on both checks. The decision model serves one request at a time, and the many pair questions queued behind it made the round slower than the one question they replaced.
- **Fold:** a plain `all` — the check holds when every promise's question is a "yes". No grouping, so a failing promise's note stands with its own reason.
- **The root's examples stay out of the evidence**, since they make nothing hold.

Parts, the cut, guarantee keys and the sentence split are unchanged; what this supersedes is the pass-only escalation and the grouped any/all fold.

## Final replay at dff3e5c0 (this head, 2026-11-20)

```
node packages/eval/src/replay-judge.ts --cases ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/meets-intent-cases.json --deployment ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/deployment.json --judge local/qwen3.8-27b --decision-model clef/clef --arm cand=. --arm base=19f6ddc9 --arm base2=19f6ddc9 --repeat 3 --concurrency 2 --escalations 4 --rows ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/rows-final-meets-intent.jsonl
node packages/eval/src/replay-judge.ts --cases ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/delivers-purpose-all.json --deployment ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/deployment.json --judge local/qwen3.8-27b --decision-model clef/clef --arm cand=. --repeat 5 --concurrency 2 --escalations 4 --rows ~/quack-lab/contracts-replay/rows-final-delivers-purpose.jsonl
```

The first command compares `meets_intent` against main, with base2 as the control arm. The second runs the 13 positives and the 5 negatives on cand.

### meets_intent — 13 cases, 3 repeats

| case | base | base2 | cand |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0ac788c4-v10 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |
| 0c200fa8-v5 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | **0 0 0** |
| 233d9ccf-v12-flipped | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |
| 233d9ccf-v13 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 0 | 1 0 1 |
| 33777f8a-v1-failed | 1 1 0 | 1 1 1 | 0 0 0 |
| 33777f8a-v32 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |
| 608df011-v11-failed | 1 1 1 | 1 0 0 | 1 1 1 |
| 608df011-v12-failed | 0 0 0 | 1 1 0 | 1 1 1 |
| 608df011-v18-failed | 0 0 0 | 0 0 0 | 0 0 0 |
| 608df011-v20 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 0 | 1 1 1 |
| aab002bf-v25 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |
| b66206df-v4 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |
| eda8542f-v10 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 | 1 1 1 |

Judge seconds per case, median: base 38.6, base2 32.9, cand 34.1 — cand inside the base spread, not slower. 27B requests per run: base 39, base2 39, cand 324 (one question per guarantee, by design at this head).

Rulings on the differences, against the contract text:

- **0c200fa8-v5, base 1×3, cand 0×3: cand is right.** Guarantee 1 ends "a variable absent from this contract is absent from the deployment environment", but the document's own root rule says "Any name not listed here is allowed only as a secret the deployment file or an extension manifest claims". A claimed-but-unlisted variable — a key the deployment file names, a store URL — is absent from the contract yet present in the environment, so the clause as written is contradicted. The fix is in the guarantee's wording, in the contract, as with the 33777f8a-v1 ruling above.
- **233d9ccf-v13, cand 1 0 1, base2 1 1 0:** the borderline "at most one event stale" guarantee; both arms flip once in three. The ruling above stands: the fix belongs in the spec.
- **33777f8a-v1, 608df011-v11 and v12:** as ruled above — cand's reading stands, and base's $ref objection is already failed by the `document_clean` and `links_resolve` code gates.
- **608df011-v20:** base2's lone flip objects that the sqlite store schema rejects a `path` the document's own example sets. Base and cand pass all three; not ruled on further.

### delivers_purpose — 13 positives and 5 negatives, 5 repeats

| case | expected | cand |
|---|---|---|
| the other 11 positive versions | yes | 5/5 |
| 0c200fa8-v5 | yes | 2/5 — known miss declared below |
| b66206df-v4 | yes | 2/5 — borderline below |
| neg1-swapped-purpose | no | 0×5 |
| neg2-added-capability | no | 0×5 (main's whole-document check: 0,0,1,1,1) |
| neg3-operation-removed | no | 1×5 — the known miss declared above, unchanged |
| neg3b-operation-gone-everywhere | no | 1×5 — the same |
| neg4-reworded | yes | 4/5 |

Judge seconds per case, median 14.5, p90 25.8.

- **New known miss (declared).** 0c200fa8-v5 fails 3 of 5 on an attribution: the purpose says the session environment is one "the distributor assembles at launch", while the document's root and `$defs/session` descriptions say "assembled by the driver at launch". The contract's own consumers list names the driver as the assembler, and the driver is the distributor's launch path — the same mechanism under two names. The one-question-per-promise shape reads all of a promise's parts together and fails the sentence on the name mismatch.
- **Borderline.** b66206df-v4 fails 3 of 5 on "state, usage, artifacts and asks use the extension SDK's settled names and payloads": the document states the shared vocabulary for `state` only. The other three's schemas reference the SDK types but no stated claim backs them; the flip-flop says borderline.

Pass criteria at this head:
- **No slower per run:** met (34.1 s inside the 32.9–38.6 base spread).
- **No more false positives:** not met as written — 0c200fa8-v5 is a new flaky false positive, declared above. Every other `met` difference is ruled on the merits above: each cand-only failure is either a true contradiction in the contract text or declared.

Compare through `met`, since some code gates fail in replay that passed on prod.

Validation at dff3e5c0, on main 19f6ddc9: CI's `check` job is green (typecheck, full test suite, sloplint). At 4ffddbb3, one commit back: `npm test` ran twice in a row, 1339 tests, 1336 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped each time; web 426 pass.
